desc: Ideation: identify that completion counts depend only on remaining parity counts and that all valid candidates at a position have equal block size.

Implement the complete Python solution for `Solution.permute` using capped factorials (cap = k + 1) and direct order-statistic unranking: compute o=(n+1)//2, e=n//2; total = fact[o]*fact[e] if n is odd else 2*fact[o]*fact[e] (capped), return [] if k > total; initialize sorted odds/evens lists; for odd n choose idx=(k-1)//(fact[o-1]*fact[e]) from odds, for even n choose idx=(k-1)//(fact[m-1]*fact[m]) from 1..n where m=n//2; update k=(k-1)%block+1 and set the required next parity; then while numbers remain, for required parity p use block = fact[count_p-1]*fact[count_other] (capped), select idx=(k-1)//block from that parity's sorted list, pop it, update k and flip parity; include safety checks for zero block or index out of range and return [] in those cases.

Test against the provided examples and brute-force all valid alternating permutations for small n (e.g., n <= 8) for all k, plus out-of-range k, edge cases n=1 and n=2, and sanity checks for large n with k=1 and k=2.
